description: A long echo with a dense allpass diffuser inside its feedback loop, so every repeat comes back smeared further than the last, with the loop broken out to a send and return

params.text: Sets the long delay, 10ms to 16 seconds; with a clock patched it becomes a ratio of that clock instead
Scales all twenty-four diffuser delays together, half to four times; below one the network is short and metallic, above two the diffuser itself rings for a couple of hundred milliseconds
Sets the allpass rotation angle: fully anticlockwise the diffuser collapses to twenty-four delays in series with silence between repeats, and the densest smear is nearer three fifths than the top
Sets the loop gain, 0% to 120%; at 100% it sustains indefinitely and past that the saturator is what holds it, so the top fifth is a drive control
Sets how much top end each pass loses, 0% to 99%, with the damping frequency held steady across sample rates
Sets the depth of the quadrature modulation on the delay inside the loop, cosine on the left and sine on the right, ±2.5ms at full; it decorrelates the repeats rather than chorusing them
Sets the rate of that modulation, 0.02Hz to 10Hz; the lamp above it blinks at that rate
Crossfades the dry and treated signals at equal power
Sets the channel rotator angle: fully anticlockwise the two channels never meet and give two independent mono echoes, and fully clockwise they are swapped at every level and trade material
Sets a slow bounded random walk on the size, nothing fully anticlockwise and ±45% over steps of half a second to four seconds fully clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to the knob above, -100% to +100%
Latches the loop frozen: the feedback goes to exactly one, the input is shut out of it, damping is bypassed and the delay time is held, crossfaded in over about 10ms
Reseeds the scattering network, giving a different room reached through the same controls; it slides into the new arrangement over about a quarter of a second rather than jumping

inputs.text: The left side of the signal to treat
The right side of the signal to treat; with nothing patched here the left jack feeds both sides
While a clock is patched here, the time knob snaps to ratios of it, from a twelfth up to twelve times, with 1 to 1 at noon, and a change lands on the next clock edge
Above its threshold the loop is frozen, and releasing it thaws; it overrides the button while it is high
A rising edge reseeds the scattering network
The left side of what comes back from whatever the send jacks were patched into; unpatched, the send is fed straight through
The right side of what comes back; unpatched it takes the left return, and with neither patched the send is fed straight through
Added to the time knob through the attenuverter beside it, ±5V for the knob's whole range

outputs.text: The left side of the feedback loop, tapped after the long delay and before the feedback gain
The right side of the feedback loop, tapped after the long delay and before the feedback gain
The left side of the treated signal crossfaded with the dry one
The right side of the treated signal crossfaded with the dry one

notes: whatever is patched between send and return is inside the loop, so it colours every repeat and its effect compounds pass after pass.
the diffuser has a length of its own, about 70ms at a size of one, so the shortest repeat interval reachable is the time setting plus that.
menu: Time change — what happens when the delay time moves: Dissolve (crossfade, as the original) or Tape (pitch-bending)
Clock sync target — what the clock jack governs: Time, or Time + rate
Freeze bypasses damping — keeps the damping out of the loop while frozen, which is what the original does
Input to loop when frozen — Muted (true freeze) or Open (feed the frozen cloud)
Reset scattering to the original — puts the prime-index scales back to the values the original algorithm uses
